parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 1.3, which is a population pyramid for the United Arab Emirates (UAE), an HIC.

![Population pyramid showing age distribution by gender. Males on the left, females on the right, ages range from 0 to 80+ years.](assets/001-population-pyramid-showing-age-distribution-by-g.png)

Most of the migration to the UAE is voluntary.

Describe the **pull factors **of HICs, such as the UAE, to migrants from LICs.
parts.solution_md:
Migrants from LICs are often attracted to HICs, such as the UAE, by better economic and social factors. One of the main pulls is higher pay and regular income **[1] **which allow migrants to support their families and send money back home as remittances **[d]**.

Migrants are also attracted by the more reliable access to essential services, including healthcare, clean water, and electricity** [1] **which leads to a better quality of life for the migrants. **[d]**

Finally, MEDCs may have more stable economies and political environments, offering migrants a sense of security. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word **'describe'** means that the answer must state the key pull factors of HICs.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - One mark **[1] **is awarded for each valid point
> - One mark** [d] **will be awarded for the development of a valid point
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of a response to this question. Other information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Improved health care.
> - Better entertainment and bright lights.
> - Better housing.

parts.problem_md:
Study **Fig. 1.2, **which is a map showing information about global net migration.

![World map showing net migration from 2010 to 2015: countries in blue have positive net migration, while those in pink have negative net migration.](assets/002-world-map-showing-net-migration-from-2010-to-201.png)

**Fig 1.2**

Explain the reasons why experience negative net migration.
parts.solution_md:
Negative net migration occurs when more people leave than arrive. One reason is unemployment or low pay, **[1] **which pushes people to move to places with better job opportunities [**d].** Poor healthcare systems, such as not having enough doctors or hospitals** [1],** encourage people to migrate for better medical services [**d]**.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word '**explain**' means that the answer should include supporting details and explanations for why an area may experience negative net migration.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - One mark** [1]**** **will be awarded for each valid point (up to a maximum of 4 marks)
> - One mark** [d] **will be awarded for the development of a valid point
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of a response to this question. Other information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - There are more emigrants than immigrants.
> - There is a lack of clean water or sanitation.
> - There is either poor education or not enough schools in the area.
> - There are earthquakes, volcanic eruptions or a tsunami.
> - There are inadequate supplies of food, electricity or water.
> - There is a famine or soil too poor to grow crops, etc.
> - There is persecution or a lack of personal freedom.
> - There is corruption, political instability, poor government or dictatorship.
> - There is genocide or a high murder rate.
> - There are high levels of pollution.

> **[exam-tip]**
> This question is focussed on push factors so pull factors will only gain credit if they are phrased as 'more' or 'better'. For example, other areas have better access to clean water.

parts.problem_md:
Study **Fig. 1.1, **which shows information about migration across the Mediterranean Sea from Libya to Italy between January 2015 and August 2016.

![Map showing migrant routes from Libya to Italy, with paths spreading across Europe. Cities like Rome, Milan, Tripoli, and Zawiya are marked.](assets/003-map-showing-migrant-routes-from-libya-to-italy-w.png)

Explain why the arrival of large numbers of migrants across the Mediterranean Sea may cause problems in Italy.
parts.solution_md:
Italy faces pressures on food supplies as local resources may not be enough to meet the needs of both residents and migrants.**[1] **Another problem is housing. **[1] **here might not be enough temporary housing for everyone, so shelters become overcrowded.** [d] **Unemployment can also rise, as migrants may struggle to find jobs in an already competitive job market, creating further economic challenges for Italy.** [1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**

> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - One mark** [1]**** **will be awarded for each valid point (up to a maximum of 4 marks)
> - One mark** [d] **will be awarded for the development of a valid point
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of a response to this question. Other information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Conflicts with or resentment of the local population.
> - The cost of providing patrols or rescue boats.
> - Lack of housing or cramped housing and spread of disease.
> - Cultural issues.

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 1.2, which shows information about Arlington County, an area in the USA. | Arlington County is home to the USA’s largest Bolivian community. In Arlington there are apartment buildings filled with people who have migrated from towns in the Cochabamba Valley in Bolivia, hence the nickname ‘Arlibamba’. There are many Bolivian restaurants and food shops, such as Pike Pizza, a converted pizza restaurant that now sells traditional Bolivian food. This is one of many meeting places for the Bolivian community. They are also places to watch the Bolivian national soccer team play games on TV.

Bolivians have formed several football leagues in the Arlington region. Over 2000 players and fans come out each Sunday to participate. Many of the teams are named after towns in Bolivia like Real Santa Cruz.

An aim of one of the Arlington football leagues is to improve life in the small villages in the Esteban Arce province of Bolivia. Most people there live off basic agriculture and remittances from abroad. Teams send their winnings back home to fund schools, infrastructure and churches. It has been estimated that villages in Bolivia received over US \$20000 a year from donations from the league. | |---| **Fig. 1.2** Assess the impact migration to the USA is likely to have on the small villages in Bolivia and the people who still live there.
parts.solution_md:
One positive impact of migration to the USA  is the reduction of pressure on services **[1] **such as healthcare, education, and food supplies, as fewer people remain in these villages **[d].**

However, migration can also cause challenges. Empty houses, shop closures, and school closures are common due to fewer residents **[1 }**.There may also be an imbalance in the age structure, with only the elderly and children remaining, leading to a higher dependent population **[1]**.

There are both positive and negative impacts of migration to the USA. Overall the positive impacts outweigh the negative.** [1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is **'assess'**; this means that the answer needs to include judgement about the relative value of trade and aid in reducing uneven development.
> 
> **Mark allocation:**
> 
> - One mark **[1]** for each positive or negative impact. (up to a maximum 4 marks)
> - One  mark** [1]** for a reasoned conclusion that shows balance.
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of a response to this question. Other information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Benefit from winnings or donations from football leagues in the USA for investment in schools, infrastructure, or churches.
> - New skills are brought back when a migrant returns.
> - Family breakdown.
> - Impact on culture, either positive or negative.
> - The village or country's economy develops.

> **[exam-tip]**
> When the question asks you to evaluate or assess it is important that to reach a final judgement to gain the full five marks.

parts.problem_md: Suggest problems that international migrants may face when settling in a new country.
parts.solution_md:
Cultural differences may be challenging  because it can be hard to get used to a new language, customs, and social norms, making international migrants feel alone or left out **[1]. **International migrants may have trouble getting work because of language barriers or because their qualifications from their home country are not recognised **[1].** Housing can also be a problem since migrants may not be able to afford homes in cities or may face discrimination from owners or neighbours **[1].** Also, it might be hard for them to get services like schooling and health care if they do not know how these systems work **[1]**.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word **‘suggest’** means that the answer needs to apply knowledge and understanding to consider the reasons international migrants may face challenges.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - One mark [1] for each valid point (up to a maximum of 4 marks)
> - One mark [d] for development of a simple point
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of a response to this question. Other information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - There is a lack of qualifications, skills or education.
> - They are not aware of minimum wage laws.
> - Jobs are low-paid or there is exploitation by employers.
> - There is a feeling of homesickness or separation from family.
> - Only poor quality housing is available.
> - There is discrimination or persecution.
> - The process of obtaining a visa is challenging.

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 1.1, which shows information about the country of origin of people living in Canada in 1990 and 2015.

![Bar chart comparing the number of immigrants (in thousands) by country of origin in 1990 and 2015, with China and India as top sources.](assets/005-bar-chart-comparing-the-number-of-immigrants-in-.png)

How many people from the USA lived in Canada in 2015?

**Extract:**

Study Fig. 1.1, which shows information about the country of origin of people living in Canada in 1990 and 2015.

Using the information from Fig. 1.1.

Describe how the number of people from China and Italy living in Canada changed between 1990 and 2015.
You should use statistics in your answer.
parts.solution_md:
The graph shows that in 1990, 170,000 more Italians than Chinese people arrived in Canada. However, in 2015, approximately 430,000 more Chinese than Italians arrived in Canada **[1]**.** **

This indicates that the total number of Chinese immigrants to Canada increased by three times, reaching a total of 540,000.  At the same time, the number of Italian immigrants to Canada decreased by 60,000 **[1]**.** **

The number of people from **Italy** **decreased **from 340,000 in 1990 to 280,000 in 2015, resulting in a total decrease of 60,000 people migrating into Canada. The number of people from **China increased **from 170,000 in 1990 to 710,000 in 2015, resulting in a total increase of 540,000 people migrating into Canada **[1]**.** **

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word **'describe'** means that the answer must state the key changes for the two groups of migrants.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - One mark [1] is awarded for use of statistics
> - One mark [1] for identifying change.
> - One mark [1] for year and country of origin

parts.problem_md: Explain why there are large amounts of migration to a country you have studied. Name of country ............................................................
parts.solution_md:
Migration from Mexico to the USA  is due to a range of push and pull factors. **[KU] **Many Mexicans are pushed to leave Mexico due to high unemployment, poverty, and crime rates.** [KU]** Arid conditions and water shortages limit farming opportunities, and natural hazards like earthquakes make life more difficult. **[KU]**

The USA attracts migrants with better job opportunities, higher wages, and a higher quality of life**. [KU]** Many find work in agriculture in border states like California and Texas, where there is a strong demand for low-skilled labour. **[KU] **Being able to send remittances back to families in Mexico is also a key motivation. **[KU]**

The location of Mexico is also important, as it shares a long border with the USA, and many migrants move to areas with existing Mexican communities, making the transition easier. **[KU]**

Over the past 40 years, this has become one of the largest migration flows in the world. **[KU]** Today, over 10.9 million Mexicans live in the USA, making up around 24% of its foreign-born population. **[KU] **

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is **‘explain’**; this means the answer needs to give a reasons for the migration flow from Mexico to the USA. This needs to be both push and pull factors.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This is a 'level of response' answer. Each point made in the answer does not equal a mark.
> 
> - AO focus = AO1 [KU]
> - A top-level 3 (7 mark) answer will use specific examples that demonstrate detailed, developed knowledge and understanding [KU] of international migration .
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of a response to this question. Other information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Health care provision
> - Quality of education
> - Food/water availability
> - Social welfare
> - Human rights.
